paragraphs: Formed in 2007, the business of what is now The Oncology Institute, Inc. ("TOI", the "Company", "we", or "our) and its affiliated professional corporations was created initially as a collection of community oncology practices in southern California, and has evolved to be a national leader in the pursuit of reducing the ever-rising cost of oncology care, while embracing clinical best practices, state-of-the-art technology, and compassionate treatment of patients.

While we continue our original purpose of seeing our patients on a fee-for-service basis for their oncology, hematology, specialty infusion, oral pharmacy needs, as well as enrolling patients in clinical trials, where appropriate, TOI's true mission lies in our differentiated ability to partner with managed care providers and other risk-bearing entities to transfer the risk and patient coordination responsibility of treating cancer in the subset of the population that is experiencing an oncology treatment episode. To do this, we utilize a combination of gain/loss sharing, capitation, and full delegation contracts at the population-level, which allow TOI to control the treatment of oncology patients in an outpatient setting, across both medical oncology (traditional IV-based infusion therapy) and radiation oncology (radiation therapy provided by linear accelerator equipment).

TOI treats patients across 17 markets and five states throughout the United States, via our 65 clinics owned by affiliated physicians and staffed with 116 providers (the "TOI PCs"), 81 independently-owned clinics which are contracted with TOI's managed services organization, as well as our contracted network of 198 independent providers unaffiliated with TOI in instances where TOI is the fully delegated market manager under a value-based contract.
Through this network, TOI managed a population of approximately 2.0 million patients under value-based agreements as of December 31, 2025.

TOI provides medical care on a fee-for service basis for physician services, in-house infusion, radiation, and innovative programs like outpatient blood product transfusions, along with 24/7 patient support. The services TOI provides in its fee for service business are generally covered under commercial and government managed care programs, which are billed retrospectively for care provided in clinics, following a typically small patient co-pay collected at the time of service. We customarily bill for physician and infusion services on a CPT-code basis, and for drugs on a cost-plus basis. We are generally reliant on outside referrals of these fee-for-service patients, who may be in the care of a primary care provider, non-oncology specialist physician, or hospitalist, who then refers the patient upon diagnosis to an oncology provider within TOI. We generate these referrals based on the reputation of our doctors and our platform within the communities we serve, as well as our active and direct referrer education efforts.

TOI offers value-based contracts to payors, including managed care organizations and other risk-bearing entities, who are interested in transferring both the risk and responsibility for managing outpatient oncology care to us. These arrangements can take multiple different forms, but typically involve a population-level assignment, where TOI receives 100% share of a patient population and is paid either a fixed amount per member on a regular (typically monthly) schedule, or, less commonly, is paid/recoups a portion of gains/losses at the end of a measurement period. In this way, TOI receives a predictable, recurring payment for oncology care, and generates a profit to the extent the actual cost of oncology care for our contracted patient populations is less than this fixed payment. Generally, we are able to offer fixed payments to payors that represent a discount to the historical oncology cost and/or cost trend for these patient populations, while still generating positive profitability for TOI. We do this through active management of clinical pathways and drug formulary, incorporating best clinical practices and recognized quality metrics, using both our affiliated and MSO clinics, as well as negotiating network contracts with third-party providers. TOI's decade-plus of experience efficiently managing oncology populations, intensive clinical interventions, and TOI's comprehensive knowledge of therapeutic options across both pharmaceuticals and radiation therapy position us to effectively manage these contracts in a way that adds value to both our payor partners and patients.

TOI operates specialty and retail pharmacies in all 5 states through which we are capable of filling medication orders that are incidental or coincidental to our patients' oncology care. Often patients undergoing outpatient oncology treatment are receiving a combination of IV-infused, oral, and injectable medications, for oncology treatment as well as other co-occurring conditions, making our populations particularly relevant for pharmacy services on therapeutics that are not provider-administered within the clinic and therefore would typically fall outside of our traditional Patient Services fee for service business. Because of the relationship derived from the repeated visits and close consultation that occurs during treatment for an active oncology episode, our patients develop a relationship to providers in the TOI clinics, as well as a cadence of regular visits. This provides TOI a complementary opportunity to service these patients by ordering and filling oral, IV, and injectable medications that the patients frequently self-administer or have administered inside or outside of TOI's clinics. For these medications, we are typically billing patients' pharmacy benefit managers, which are generally incorporated within patients' managed care plans, whether commercial or government. Pharmacy claims are generally billed at the time medication is ordered, along with a customary patient co-pay, which TOI seeks to collect at the time of pickup. Reimbursement for the pharmacy is generally calculated using a wholesale acquisition cost, or WAC-minus basis, which is on average a higher rate than TOI is able to procure the medication from its vendors.

Through TOI Clinical Research, LLC ("TCR"), the clinical research arm of our affiliated professional corporations, or TOI PCs, we also provide and manage clinical trial services and research for the benefit of cancer patients, as well as palliative care for patients in the last stages of disease. Many of our services, such as managing clinical trials and palliative care programs, are traditionally accessed through academic and tertiary care settings, while the TOI PCs bring these services to patients in a community setting, by which we mean, providing care in our convenient clinic locations rather than academic or tertiary care settings. Revenue in our clinical trials business is billed to pharmaceutical companies or the contract research organizations engaged by pharmaceutical companies to administer their trials, and paid in arrears based on which individual medical procedures were performed on enrolled patients during the course of the trial. See Note 1 of the consolidated financial statements for the profit sharing arrangement TOI entered into in 2025 with Helios Clinical Research.

As a value-based oncology company, we seek to deliver better quality care while managing costs for patients and payors that we serve. We define value-based care as care that focuses on providing optimal health outcomes and healthcare affordability and a value-based contract as any contract that removes the incentive to drive up cost of care or overutilization, while rewarding better clinical outcomes, cost and quality. We work to accomplish this goal by reducing wasteful, inefficient or futile care that drives up costs but does not improve outcomes. We believe payors and employers are aligned with the value-based model due to its enhanced access, improved outcomes, and lower costs. Patients under our affiliated providers' care can benefit from evidence-based and personalized care plans, gain access to sub-specialized care in convenient community

locations, and lower out-of-pocket costs. We believe our affiliated providers enjoy the stability and predictability of a large multi-state practice, are not incentivized or pressured to over-treat when it may be inconsistent with a patient's goals of care and can focus on practicing outstanding evidence-based oncology care.

In contrast to value-based care, we believe much of traditional fee-for-service, or FFS, oncology care is plagued by misaligned incentives that drive up costs and often lower the quality of care. In FFS care, oncologists are reimbursed on a "cost-plus" basis for drugs which in turn are often responsible for the majority of a practice's revenue. This "cost-plus" model may incentivize oncologists to prescribe the most expensive treatments even if lower cost alternatives that are still medically appropriate are available, as well as to continue to utilize chemotherapy in advanced cancer patients who may no longer benefit from such treatment. In these cases, patients and payors not only bear the burden of higher cost of care, but patients may also suffer negative health outcomes including higher rates of emergency room visits and hospitalizations for supportive care needs due to the side effects associated with chemotherapy.

In 2025, we generated more than 46% of our revenue from patients who are covered by value-based contracts. Historically, our value-based contracts have predominantly taken the form of capitated contracts. Our capitated contracts remove incentives to drive up costs, and they also have incentives for meeting or exceeding certain quality metrics. In some capitated contracts we are penalized if we fail to meet certain quality metrics. In other capitated contracts, we receive bonuses/rewards if we meet or exceed certain quality metrics. Our value-based contracts could also take on other forms, such as sharing with payors in the cost savings generated for specific medical oncology costs (which we refer to as 'gain-sharing' contracts), along with incentives to meet certain quality metrics. These contracts, despite their modifications on how reimbursement is structured, still meet the definition of value-based care. We and our affiliated providers have contractual relationships with payors serving a variety of patients, including Medicare Advantage ("MA"), Medicaid, and commercial patients. These payors include affiliates of Anthem, CareMore Health, Heritage Provider Network and Optum Care.

In 2025, we continued to evolve the way we structure our value-based arrangements, particularly in areas of the country where there is an increased desire and capability from managed care groups to fully delegate traditional managed care services for the treatment of oncology to providers like TOI. Under this model, which we refer to as "full delegation" TOI performs not only the traditional function of care provider for a portion of patients, but also functions more classically executed by the managed care industry, including utilization management, network construction, and claims adjudication. Under this full delegation model, TOI is paid a capitation by the payor on a similar per-member, per-month basis as TOI's traditional capitation model. Using these funds, TOI is then responsible for management of the oncology care for patients seen at both TOI clinics, as well as at independent clinics within the network constructed and managed by TOI. With both TOI and network providers, TOI is responsible for authorizing and paying relevant claims. We believe that these new contracting methodologies are furthering our mission to provide access to world-class oncology care, in an affordable manner, to underserved populations, allowing us to be an even more engaged partner to our payors for populations beyond those serviced directly in a TOI clinic.

We believe that our position in the market and focus on elevating the state of oncology care with a value-based care model positions our affiliated providers well for future growth. Our technology platform supports this growth and enables the TOI PCs to standardize and deliver consistent value-based care at scale. We believe that our model will support growth into new markets, and allow us to continue to service more patients across the United States.

("TOI") along with its consolidating subsidiaries (the "Company"). All dollar values are expressed in thousands, unless otherwise noted.

Unless the context dictates otherwise, references in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to the "Company," "we," "us," "our," and similar words are references to The Oncology Institute, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("TOI"), and its consolidated subsidiaries and affiliated entities, as appropriate, including its consolidated variable interest entities ("VIEs").

The Company is a leading value-based oncology company that manages community-based oncology practices for the Company and for independent oncology practices that together serve patients across 17 markets and five states throughout the United States. As of December 31, 2025, we operate 65 community-based oncology practices, staffed with 116 oncologists and advanced practice providers employed by our affiliated physician-owned professional corporations, referred to as the "TOI PCs." In addition to our TOI-affiliated providers, we also manage a network of 207 providers in Florida under the Florida Oncology Network brand. Collectively across the provider base, we manage a population of approximately 2.0 million patients under value-based agreements as of December 31, 2025. The Company's mission is to heal and empower cancer patients through compassion, innovation, and state-of-the-art medical care.

Operationally, the Company's medical centers provide a complete suite of medical oncology services including: physician services, in-house infusion, in-house specialty pharmacy, clinical trials, radiation therapy, educational seminars, support groups, counseling, and 24/7 patient assistance. Many of our services, such as managing clinical trials and palliative care programs, are traditionally accessed through academic and tertiary care settings, while the TOI PCs bring these services to patients in a community setting. As scientific research progresses and more treatment options become available, cancer care is shifting from acute care episodes to chronic disease management. With this shift, it is increasingly important for high-quality, high-value cancer care to be available in a local community setting to all patients in need.

As a value-based oncology company, the Company seeks to deliver both better quality care and lower cost of care for payors and patients. The Company works to accomplish this goal by reducing wasteful, inefficient or counterproductive care that drives up costs but does not improve outcomes. The Company believes payors and employers are aligned with the value-based model due to its enhanced access, improved outcomes, and lower costs. Patients under the Company's affiliated providers' care can benefit from evidence-based and personalized care plans, gain access to sub-specialized care in convenient community locations, and lower out-of-pocket costs. The Company believes its affiliated providers enjoy the stability and predictability of a large multi-state practice, are not incentivized or pressured to overtreat when it may be inconsistent with a patient's goals of care, and can focus on practicing outstanding evidence-based medicine, rather than business building.

Additionally, we allow our independent network participating providers to access the ability to treat patient populations that are managed under value-based care contracts without the need to incur costs required to build clinical or operational infrastructure typical for risk-bearing entities, or to adopt new operational frameworks which may be disruptive to their existing practices.

The Company receives payments from the following sources for services rendered: (i) commercial insurers; (ii) pharmacy benefit managers ("PBMs"), (iii) the federal government under the Medicare program administered by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services ("CMS"); (iv) state governments under Medicaid and other programs; (v) other third-party payors and managed care organizations (e.g., risk bearing organizations and independent practice associations ("IPAs"); and (vi) individual patients and clients.

Revenue primarily consists of capitation revenue, fee-for-service ("FFS") revenue, specialty pharmacy revenue, and clinical trials revenue. Capitation and FFS revenue comprise the revenues within the Company's patient services segment and are presented together in the results of operations. The following paragraphs provide a summary of the principal forms of our billing arrangements and how revenue is recognized for each type of revenue.

Capitation revenues consist primarily of fees for medical services provided by the TOI PCs or network providers to the Company's patients under a capitated arrangement with various risk-bearing medical groups or managed care organizations. Capitation revenue is paid monthly based on the number of enrollees by the contracted payor (per member per month or "PMPM"). Capitation contracts generally have a legal term of one year or longer. Payments in capitation contracts are variable since they primarily include PMPM fees associated with unspecified membership that fluctuates throughout the term of the contract; however, based on our experience, our total underlying membership generally increases over time as penetration of Medicare Advantage products grows and our payor partners, who tend to be the larger and more sophisticated operators within the industry, consolidate. Certain contracts include terms for a capitation deduction where the cost of out-of-network referrals of members are deducted from the future payment. Revenue is recognized in the month services are rendered on the basis of the transaction price established at that time.

FFS revenue represents revenue earned under contracts in which we bill and collect for specific medical services rendered by the TOI PCs' employed physicians. The terms for FFS contracts are short in duration and only last for the period over which services are rendered (typically, one day). FFS revenue consists of fees for medical services provided to patients. As specialist providers, our FFS revenue is dependent on referrals from other physicians, such as primary care physicians. The Company's affiliated providers build trusted, professional relationships with these physicians and their associated medical groups, which can lead to recurring FFS volume; however, this volume is subject to numerous factors the Company cannot control and can fluctuate over time. The Company also receives FFS revenue for capitated patients that receive medical services which are excluded from the Company's capitation contracts. Under the FFS arrangements, third-party payors and patients are billed for patient care services provided by the TOI PCs. Payments for services provided are generally less than billed charges. The Company records revenue net of an allowance for contractual adjustments, which represents the net revenue expected to be collected from third-party payors (including managed care, commercial, and governmental payors such as Medicare and Medicaid), and patients. These expected collections are based on fees and negotiated payment rates in the case of third-party payors, the specific benefits provided for under each patient's healthcare plan, mandated payment rates in the case of Medicare and Medicaid programs, and historical gross charges and cash collections (net of recoveries). The recognition of net revenue (gross charges less contractual allowances) from such services is dependent on certain factors, such as the proper completion of medical charts following a patient visit, the forwarding of such charts to our billing center for medical coding and entering into the Company's billing system, and the verification of each patient's submission or representation at the time services are rendered as to the payor(s) responsible for payment of such services. Revenue is recorded on the date the services are rendered based on the information known at the time of entering of such information into the Company's billing systems as well as an estimate of the revenue associated with medical services.

Oral prescription drugs prescribed by doctors to their patients are sold directly through the TOI PCs' dispensaries and our retail pharmacies. Revenue for the prescriptions is based on fee schedules set by various PBMs and other third-party payors.

The TOI PCs also enter into contracts to perform clinical research trials. The terms for clinical trial contracts last many months as the clinical research is performed. Each contract represents a single, integrated set of research activities that are

satisfied over time as the output of results from the trial is captured for the trial sponsor to review. Under the clinical trial contracts, the TOI PCs receive a fixed payment for administrative, set-up, and close-down fees; a fixed amount for each patient site visit; and certain expense reimbursements. The Company recognizes revenue for these arrangements on the fees earned to date based on the state of the trial, as established under contract with the customer. On March 31, 2025, the Company entered into a Research Services Agreement ("RSA") with Helios CR, Inc. ("Helios"), effective May 5, 2025, pursuant to which the Clinical Trials segment is operated by Helios in its entirety under a profit sharing arrangement with the Company. As part of the RSA, there is a Transition Services Agreement, in which certain administrative and professional services are provided by Helios for a certain period of time. Additionally, the Company pays a management fee to Helios on a periodic basis for certain shared services.

Direct costs - patient services primarily includes chemotherapy drug costs, clinician salaries and benefits, and medical supplies. Clinicians include oncologists, advanced practice providers such as physician assistants and nurse practitioners, and registered nurses employed by the TOI PCs.

paragraphs: 於2007年成立，現為The Oncology Institute, Inc.（"TOI"、"公司"、"我們"或"我們的"）及其附屬專業公司所從事的業務，最初是以南加州社區腫瘤醫療診所為起點，並已發展成為美國在降低持續上升的腫瘤照護成本方面的重要領導者，同時也採用臨牀最佳實務、最先進的科技與對病患的關懷治療。

雖然我們持續履行最初的宗旨，即以費用服務方式為病患提供腫瘤、血液學、專科輸液及口服藥物需求的照護，並在適當的情況下為病患入組臨牀試驗，但TOI真正的使命在於我們獨特的能力，能與風險承擔者合作，例如管理照護提供者，將治療癌症的風險與病患協調責任轉移至正在接受腫瘤治療的特定人口羣體。為達成此目標，我們透過在人口層級使用的獲利/虧損分享、定額給付及全權委託契約，讓TOI能在門診環境中控制腫瘤病患的治療，涵蓋醫療腫瘤學（傳統靜脈輸液治療）與放射腫瘤學（透過線性加速器設備提供的放射治療）。
TOI透過我們65間由附屬醫生所有並由116位醫療人員（"TOI PCs"）服務的診所，以及81間獨立所有並與TOI管理服務組織簽約的診所，以及在TOI為價值契約下的完全委託市場管理者的場合，與我們的198間獨立醫療人員簽約的網路，於美國17個市場及5個州為病患提供照護服務。
透過此網路，截至2025年12月31日，TOI已透過價值契約管理約2.0百萬名病患。

TOI 提供以費用為基礎的醫療照護服務，包括醫生服務、內部輸液、放射治療以及創新方案如門診血液製品輸血，並提供 24/7 病患支援。TOI 提供的費用為基礎服務，通常被商業及政府管理照護計畫所涵蓋，這些計畫會在診所提供照護後，回溯計費，並通常收取少量的病患共付金。我們通常以 CPT 編碼方式計費醫生及輸液服務，並以成本加成方式計費藥物。我們通常依賴外部轉介這些費用為基礎的病患，這些病患可能正在接受一般科醫生、非腫瘤科專科醫生或住院醫生的照護，並在診斷後轉介至 TOI 內的腫瘤科醫生。我們透過醫生的聲譽及我們在服務社區中的平台，以及我們積極且直接的轉介教育努力來產生這些轉介。

TOI 向支付者提供價值為基礎的契約，包括管理照護組織和其他風險承擔機構，這些機構希望將門診腫瘤照護的風險與責任轉移給我們。這些安排可以有多種不同的形式，但通常涉及人口層面的指派，TOI 會獲得某個病患人口羣體的 100% 管理權，並根據定期（通常為每月）的排程，以固定金額每名會員的方式獲取報酬，或較少見的是，在測量週期結束時，根據獲利或虧損的部份進行報酬或回收。透過這種方式，TOI 會獲得可預測且持續的門診腫瘤照護報酬，並在實際的腫瘤照護成本低於此固定報酬時產生利潤。我們通常能為支付者提供固定報酬，這些報酬代表歷史腫瘤照護成本及/或這些病患羣體的成本趨勢的折扣，同時仍能為 TOI 產生正向的利潤。我們透過積極管理臨牀路徑及藥物形式ulary，結合最佳臨牀實踐及被認可的品質指標，使用我們的附屬及 MSO 醫院，以及與第三方提供者談判網路契約來做到這一點。TOI 在管理腫瘤羣體、強化臨牀幹預及對藥物及放射治療的全面知識方面擁有十年以上的經驗，使我們能有效地管理這些契約，為支付者及病患創造價值。

TOI 在所有 5 個州運營專業及零售藥房，這些州是我們能夠填寫與病患腫瘤照護相關的藥物訂單的州。許多正在接受門診腫瘤治療的病患同時會接受 IV 注射、口服及注射藥物，用於腫瘤治療及其他同時存在的疾病，使我們的羣體對非由醫療機構提供的藥物治療服務特別相關。由於在治療活躍的腫瘤病例期間會有重複造訪及密切諮詢的關係，我們的病患會與 TOI 醫院的醫療團隊建立關係，並形成定期造訪的習慣。這為 TOI 提供了補充性的機會，為這些病患訂購並填發他們經常自行注射或在 TOI 醫院內外注射的口服、IV 及注射藥物。對於這些藥物，我們通常會向病患的藥物福利管理機構計費，這些機構通常包含在病患的管理照護計畫中，無論是商業或政府機構。藥物申領通常在藥物訂購時計費，並搭配常見的病患共付金，TOI 會在取藥時收取。藥物報銷通常根據整批採購成本（Wholesale Acquisition Cost, WAC）或 WAC 減去的基礎計算，這通常比 TOI 從供應商處購入藥物的價格高出。

透過 TOI Clinical Research, LLC（"TCR"），即我們附屬專業公司（TOI PCs）的臨牀研究部門，我們也為癌症病患提供並管理臨牀試驗服務及研究，以及為處於疾病末期的病患提供緩和醫療。許多我們的服務，例如管理臨牀試驗及緩和醫療計畫，傳統上是透過學術及三級醫療機構提供的，而 TOI PCs 則將這些服務帶到社區環境中，即在我們方便的診所內提供照護，而非學術或三級醫療機構環境。我們臨牀試驗業務的收入會計給藥物製造商或由藥物製造商聘請的合同研究機構，並根據試驗期間 enrolle 患者所接受的個別醫療程序進行後付計費。請參閱合併財務報表的附註 1，以瞭解 TOI 在 2025 年與 Helios Clinical Research 籤訂的利潤分享協議。

作為一家以價值為本的腫瘤學公司，我們致力於為所服務的病人與付費者提供更優質的照護，同時管理成本。我們將價值為本的照護定義為專注於提供最佳健康結果與醫療可負擔性，而價值為本的契約則指任何能消除驅動醫療成本上升或過度使用醫療資源的動機，同時獎勵更佳臨牀結果、成本與品質的契約。我們透過減少浪費、低效率或無效的照護，來達成此目標，這些照護會提高成本但不會改善結果。我們相信付費者與僱主會與價值為本的模式一致，因其具有更高的可近性、改善的結果與較低的成本。在本公司合作醫療機構照護下的病人，可受益於基於證據與個人化照護計畫，獲得便利社區內的次專科照護，並享有較低的自付費用。

與價值為本的照護相對，我們認為傳統的費用為本（Fee-for-Service, FFS）腫瘤學照護，因動機不一致而常導致成本上升與照護品質降低。在費用為本的照護中，腫瘤學者根據「成本加成」方式獲得藥物補償，而藥物往往佔據診所收入的絕大多數。這種「成本加成」模式可能促使腫瘤學者開立最昂貴的治療方式，即使有較低成本且仍符合醫療適應症的替代方案可用，也會持續使用化療於晚期癌症病人，這些病人可能已無法從化療中受益。在這些情況下，病人與付費者不僅要承擔更高的照護成本，病人也可能面臨負面健康結果，包括更高的急診室就診與因化療副作用而需要住院的支援性照護需求。

2025年，我們來自價值為本契約病人的收入超過46%。歷來，我們的價值為本契約主要以資本化契約形式存在。資本化契約會消除驅動成本上升的動機，同時也有達成或超越特定品質指標的激勵措施。在某些資本化契約中，我們若未能達成特定品質指標，將會被處罰。在其他資本化契約中，我們若達成或超越特定品質指標，則會獲得獎金或獎勵。我們的價值為本契約也可能以其他形式存在，例如與付費者共享特定醫療腫瘤學成本所產生的成本節省（我們稱為「獲利共享」契約），以及達成特定品質指標的激勵措施。這些契約，儘管在補償結構上有所調整，仍符合價值為本照護的定義。我們與本公司合作醫療機構與多種病人有契約關係，包括醫療保險優化（"MA"）、醫療救助（Medicaid）與商業病人。這些付費者包括安泰（Anthem）、CareMore Health、Heritage Provider Network 和 Optum Care 的附屬機構。

2025年，我們持續改進價值為本安排的結構方式，特別是在一些地區，管理照護機構對將傳統管理照護服務完全委託給像 TOI 這樣的醫療機構有更高的需求與能力。在這種模式下，我們稱為「完全委託」，TOI 不僅執行傳統的照護提供者功能，還執行更多傳統由管理照護產業執行的功能，包括使用管理、網路建設與申報審核。在這種完全委託模式下，TOI 會根據與傳統資本化模式相似的每會員每月基礎，由付費者支付資本化費用。利用這些資金，TOI 會負責管理在 TOI 醫療中心及 TOI 建設與管理的獨立醫療中心所見的腫瘤學照護。在 TOI 與網路醫療機構之間，TOI 會負責核准並支付相關申報。我們相信這些新的契約方法有助於我們實現使命，為未被服務的羣體提供可負擔的優質腫瘤學照護，使我們成為付費者更積極的合作夥伴，服務的對象不僅限於 TOI 醫療中心直接服務的病人。

於 2025 年，我們持續進化我們結構價值型安排的方式，特別是在國家某些地區，這些地區的 managed care 羣體有更高的意願與能力，將傳統的 managed care 服務完全委託給像 TOI 這樣的提供者，用以治療腫瘤學。在這種模式下，我們稱之為 "full delegation"，TOI 不僅執行傳統的照護提供者功能，為部分病患服務，同時也執行較傳統由 managed care 行業執行的功能，包括使用管理、網路建設與申報審核。在這種 full delegation 模式下，TOI 會根據與 TOI 傳統 capitation 模式相似的每名會員每月基礎，由 payor 支付 capitation。利用這些資金，TOI 則負責管理在 TOI 醫院所見的腫瘤學照護，以及在 TOI 建設與管理的網路內獨立醫院所見的病患。對於 TOI 與網路提供者，TOI 會負責授權與支付相關申報。我們認為這些新的契約方法有助於我們實現使命，以可負擔的方式提供世界級的腫瘤學照護，給未被充分服務的羣體，使我們成為 payor 的更積極夥伴，服務那些不直接在 TOI 醫院服務的羣體。
我們相信我們在市場上的地位與專注於以價值為本的照護模式提升腫瘤學照護的狀態，使我們的合作醫療機構為未來的成長做好準備。我們的科技平台支持此成長，並使 TOI 醫療中心能標準化並大規模提供一致的價值為本照護。我們相信此模式將支持我們進入新市場，並使我們能持續服務更多美國病人。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析提供資訊，管理階層認為此資訊與評估及瞭解本公司（"TOI"）及其合併子公司（"公司"）整體營運成果與財務狀況相關。討論應與歷史經審計年度財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀，該財務報表為截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日之年度財務報表，並包含於本年度報告其他部分。本討論中所包含之內容為根據1933年證券法（經修正，"證券法"）第27A節及1934年證券交易法（經修正，"證券交易法"）第21E節所定義之預測性陳述。這些陳述係基於目前預期，以及管理階層的信念與假設，並涉及高度風險與不確定性。本討論中任何非歷史事實之陳述，可能被視為預測性陳述。包含"相信"、"預期"、"計畫"、"期望"、"意圖"等詞彙，用以表達未來事件或結果之不確定性之陳述，為預測性陳述。我們實際結果可能與本討論或建議之預測性陳述有重大差異。導致此差異之因素包括本年度報告第10-K表單之"風險因素"部分所描述者，以及我們隨後向證券交易委員會提交之文件中所討論之新風險，這些風險在本年度報告時點尚未出現。此外，由於這些及其他因素，我們過去之財務表現不應被視為未來表現之指標。本文件中所有預測性陳述均基於我們在本年度報告第10-K表單提交日所掌握之資訊，我們不承擔更新任何預測性陳述或說明我們實際結果可能與預測性陳述有差異之原因之義務。所有金額均以千美元為單位，除非另有說明。
除非上下文另有明確指示，否則本年度報告第10-K表單中提及的"公司"、"我們"、"我們"、"我們"及類似詞彙，均指The Oncology Institute, Inc.（"TOI"），一間德拉瓦州公司，及其合併子公司與附屬機構，如適用，包括其合併之特殊利益實體（"VIEs"）。

本公司為一領導價值導向之腫瘤學公司，管理社區基層之腫瘤學診所，為本公司及獨立之腫瘤學診所服務，共同為美國17個市場及五個州之患者提供服務。截至2025年12月31日，我們經營65家社區基層之腫瘤學診所，並聘有116位腫瘤學醫師及高階專業人員，由我們附屬之醫師所有專業公司所僱用，稱為"TOI PCs"。除了我們TOI附屬之專業人員外，我們亦管理一個在佛羅裏達州之207位專業人員網路，品牌為Florida Oncology Network。總體而言，在專業人員基礎上，我們管理約2.0百萬位患者，根據價值導向之協議，截至2025年12月31日。本公司之使命為透過同情、創新與最先進之醫療照護，治療並賦能癌症患者。

營運方面，本公司之醫療中心提供完整的醫療腫瘤學服務，包括：醫師服務、院內靜脈注射、院內專門藥房、臨牀試驗、放射治療、教育講座、支持團體、諮商及24/7患者協助。許多我們之服務，例如管理臨牀試驗與緩和醫療計畫，傳統上為學術及三級醫療設施所提供，而TOI PCs則將這些服務帶入社區中，提供給患者。隨著科學研究的進步與更多治療選擇的出現，癌症照護正從急性照護事件轉向慢性疾病管理。隨著此轉變，為所有有需要之患者在當地社區設置高品質、高價值之癌症照護變得越來越重要。

作為一家價值導向之腫瘤學公司，本公司致力於為支付者與患者提供更優質之照護與更低廉之照護成本。本公司透過減少浪費、低效率或反效果之照護，以降低成本而不改善結果，來達成此目標。本公司相信支付者與僱主因價值導向模式提供增強之存取性、改善之結果與更低廉之成本，而與此模式一致。在本公司附屬專業人員照護之下之患者，可受益於基於證據與個人化之照護計畫，獲得便利社區地點之次專門化照護，並降低自付費用。本公司相信其附屬專業人員享有大型跨州診所之穩定與可預測性，不會因與患者照護目標不一致而被鼓勵或壓力過度治療，並能專注於實踐優質之基於證據之醫療，而非業務拓展。
此外，我們允許我們獨立網路參與之專業人員，無需承擔建設風險承擔實體通常所需之臨牀或營運基礎設施之成本，或採用可能幹擾其現有營運模式之新營運架構，即可接觸管理於價值導向照護契約下之患者羣。
本公司從以下來源獲得服務之報酬：(i) 商業保險公司；(ii) 藥物福利管理機構（"PBMs"）；(iii) 美國聯邦政府根據由醫療保險與醫療援助服務中心（"CMS"）管理之醫療保險計畫；(iv) 各州政府根據醫療援助及其他計畫；(v) 其他第三方支付者及管理照護組織（例如風險承擔組織及獨立診所協會（"IPAs"））；以及(vi) 個人患者及客戶。
收入主要由資本收入、按服務收費（"FFS"）收入、專門藥房收入及臨牀試驗收入組成。資本收入與按服務收費收入為本公司患者服務分部之收入，並在營運成果中共同呈現。以下段落提供我們主要收費安排之總結，以及每種收入類型如何認列收入。

資本化收入主要為 TOI 電腦或網路供應商為本公司病患提供醫療服務所收取的費用，此費用係根據與各風險承擔醫療團體或管理式照護機構所訂立的資本化安排。資本化收入每月支付一次，支付金額根據 contracted payor 所訂定的 enrollees 數量（每人每月或 "PMPM"）。資本化合約通常具有法律效力為一年或更長的期限。資本化合約的付款為變動性，因為其主要包含與未指定會員資格相關的 PMPM 費用，而此會員資格在合約期間會有所波動；然而，根據我們的經驗，我們的總體基礎會員數量通常會隨時間增加，因 Medicare Advantage 產品的滲透率提高，且我們的 payor 合作夥伴（傾向為業內較大且成熟的運營者）會進行合併。某些合約包含資本化扣除條款，其中成員的非網路轉介成本會從未來付款中扣除。收入在服務提供當月確認，依據當時所確定的交易價格。

FFS 收入為根據合約所產生的收入，我們會為 TOI 電腦所僱用醫生所提供的特定醫療服務進行開票與收款。FFS 合約的期限較短，僅持續至服務提供期間（通常為一天）。FFS 收入為提供給病患的醫療服務費用。作為專科服務提供者，我們的 FFS 收入依賴其他醫生（如一般科醫生）的轉介。本公司的相關提供者會與這些醫生及其相關醫療團體建立信任且專業的關係，這可能導致持續性的 FFS 服務量；然而，此服務量會受到許多本公司無法控制的因素影響，並可能隨時間而波動。本公司也會為根據資本化合約排除的資本化病患所接受的醫療服務收取 FFS 收入。在 FFS 安排下，第三方付款者與病患會為 TOI 電腦所提供的病患照護服務進行開票。服務提供的付款通常低於開票金額。本公司會記錄收入淨額，扣除合同調整允許的金額，這代表預期從第三方付款者（包括管理式照護、商業及政府付款者，如 Medicare 和 Medicaid）和病患收取的淨收入。這些預期收款是根據第三方付款者的費用和協議付款率、每位病患醫療計畫所提供的特定福利、Medicare 和 Medicaid 計畫的規定付款率，以及歷史總開票金額和現金收款（扣除追償）來計算。從這些服務中確認淨收入（總開票金額減去合同允許的金額）取決於某些因素，例如患者訪問後正確完成醫療記錄、將這些記錄轉送至我們的開票中心進行醫療編碼並輸入本公司開票系統、以及驗證每位患者在服務提供時所提交或表示的付款責任方。收入在服務提供當日確認，依據進入本公司開票系統時所知的資訊以及與醫療服務相關收入的預估。
醫生為其病患處方的口服處方藥品，會直接透過 TOI 電腦的藥房及我們的零售藥房進行銷售。處方藥的收入基於各 PBMs 及其他第三方付款者所設定的費用表。
TOI 電腦也會與第三方簽訂合約以執行臨牀研究試驗。臨牀試驗合約的期限通常為數個月，因為臨牀研究的執行需要較長時間。每個合約代表一組整合的研發活動，

隨著試驗結果的產生而逐步完成，供試驗機構審閱。根據臨牀試驗合約，TOI 電腦會收取固定付款，用以支付行政、設置及結案費用；每名受試者訪問的固定金額；以及某些費用補償。本公司會根據合約與客戶所訂定的試驗階段，確認這些安排的收入，基於已賺取的費用。2025 年 3 月 31 日，本公司與 Helios CR, Inc.（"Helios"）簽訂了一項研究服務協議（"RSA"），該協議自 2025 年 5 月 5 日生效，根據此協議，臨牀試驗分部由 Helios 全面運作，並與本公司訂有獲利分享安排。根據 RSA，有一項過渡服務協議，其中 Helios 會在特定期間內提供某些行政及專業服務。此外，本公司會定期向 Helios 支付管理費用，以補償某些共享服務。
直接成本 - 病患服務主要包含化療藥物成本、醫療人員薪資及福利，以及醫療用品。醫療人員包括腫瘤科醫生、高階專業人員（如醫生助理及護理師）及由 TOI 電腦僱用的註冊護理師。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的成長策略依賴我們能否建立或取得新的 TOI 電腦診所以履行我們的契約並治療我們的病患。
我們曾經經歷，並可能持續經歷快速成長與組織變動，這已對我們的管理階層與運營及財務資源造成重大壓力，並可能持續造成同樣的壓力。
我們有淨虧損的歷史，我們預期未來支出將增加，我們可能無法達成或維持獲利。
美國或全球爆發疫情、流行病或傳染病的疫情，包括 COVID-19 疫情的再次出現，可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們的服務集中於某些地理區域與人口羣，使我們面臨當地福利成本、賠償率、競爭與經濟條件不利變動的風險。
如果我們無法吸引新病患，我們的收入成長將受到不利影響。
我們主要依賴第三方付款機構的賠償，以及個人的付款，這可能會導致賠償程序出現延遲與不確定性。
政府補助金率降低或有關政府醫療衛生計畫規則的變更，可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
我們無法預測醫療改革及其他政府計畫變更對我們業務、財務狀況或營運成果的影響。
通貨膨脹可能透過增加藥品、臨牀試驗及研究、行政及其他營運成本，對我們產生不利影響。
從基於體量的補償模式轉向基於價值的補償模式，可能對我們的營運產生重大不利影響。
患者付款者結構的變更及計畫間整併可能導致補償率下降，可能對我們的收入及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們面臨來自其他醫療服務提供者的重大競爭。我們若無法有效競爭，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 我們營運於一個快速變化的環境中，涉及許多風險。我們的營運及財務結果受到各種風險與不確定性影響，包括以下所列的風險與不確定性。您應仔細考慮以下所列的風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告表10-K中包含的其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，以及我們其他公開提交至證券交易委員會的資料。以下所列的風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險。我們可能還會面臨其他未預見或目前認為不具重大影響的風險與不確定性，這些因素可能對我們的業務產生重大負面影響。以下所列的風險與不確定性反映本公司對可能對本公司及其證券產生重大負面影響的事項的觀點與看法。提及過去事件僅為說明之用，並非完整列出或表示這些因素是否已發生過或未來是否會發生的說明。如果任何下列風險或其他未說明的風險實現，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大負面影響。在此情況下，我們普通股的交易價格可能下跌。
以下為可能對The Oncology Institute, Inc. ("TOI", "we", 或 "our") 及其業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大負面影響的風險與不確定性摘要。您應配合以下完整的風險因素討論內容一起閱讀此摘要：
• 我們的成長策略依賴我們能否建立或取得診所以履行我們的契約並治療我們的病患。
• 我們已經歷，且可能持續經歷快速成長與組織變動，這已對我們的管理層及營運與財務資源產生重大壓力，且可能持續產生此種壓力。
• 我們有淨虧損的歷史，預期未來支出將增加，且我們可能無法達成或維持獲利。
• 美國或全球爆發疫情、流行病或傳染病的疫情，包括 COVID-19 疫情的再次出現，可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
